events.region: Canyon Grassland of Wallowa County; Southeast Washington Grande Ronde Valley
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
...The upper level low offshore will shift to the east just
enough to allow for monsoonal moisture to move into the region.
Instability will accompany the moisture and allow for increased
chances of isolated to scattered thunderstorms across central
Oregon and portions of the eastern mountains. Brief heavy
downpours, gusty outflow winds, small hail, and frequent
lightning will be possible...

The National Weather Service in Pendleton has issued a Red Flag
Warning for abundant lightning, which is in effect from 1 PM this
afternoon to 9 PM PDT this evening.

* AFFECTED AREA...Fire Weather Zones 693 Canyon Grasslands of
Wallowa County and 693 Southeast Washington Grande Ronde
Valley.

* TIMING...From 1 PM this afternoon to 9 PM PDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Any fire that develops will catch and spread
quickly. Outdoor burning is not recommended.

* THUNDERSTORMS...Isolated to scattered dry thunderstorms
Thursday after 1200.

* OUTFLOW WINDS...Gusts from 25-45 mph

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
...The National Weather Service in Corpus Christi has issued a Flood
Warning for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River Near Three Rivers affecting Live Oak County.

For the Nueces River...including Cotulla, Tilden, Three Rivers,
Mathis, Bluntzer, Calallen...Major flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Nueces River near Three Rivers.

* WHEN...From Monday evening until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 35.0 feet, Major lowland flooding occurs. Flow backs
up minor creeks to the slabs of lowest homes in the River Creek
Acres Subdivision, five miles southeast of George West, requiring
evacuations. Livestock are cut off and could drown in low areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:15 AM CDT Thursday the stage was 1.3 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 20.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage Monday
evening and continue rising to 33.7 feet Tuesday morning.
Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 25.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 34.1
feet on 10/08/2017.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
